data.summary: adopt / hooks install run from a LINKED git worktree of ddflow (agent shells here have PYTHONPATH=':' so cwd's code is imported) write that worktree's path into the target project's .mcp.json and git hooks; the worktree is removed on merge, after which the MCP server cannot import and every hook fails closed. Nothing says so.

data.body: Found onboarding home-simulator 2026-09-29. Probe: PYTHONPATH=<ddflow linked worktree> ddflow adopt --agents claude in a fresh repo writes PYTHONPATH=<worktree> into .mcp.json and .git/hooks/pre-commit. Redirecting silently to the primary checkout would make ddflow's own tests exercise the wrong code (hooks spawned by tests), so: detect a linked worktree (its .git is a gitdir file) and append a NOTE naming the path and the primary checkout to re-run from. Regression test: package parent in a linked worktree -> adopt output carries the note; fails on current code.
data.title: adopt and hooks install say when the path they register is a linked worktree that will be removed (fixes bug B-adopt-worktree-path)

data.title: Onboarding an existing project is one conversation: attach the MCP, and the agent drives preflight, setup, import, workflow cutover and verification WITH the operator

data.body: Stages, each with its operator question: 0 preflight (leftover worktrees/branches/stashes: merged -> remove with OK, unmerged -> recover), 1 setup from the PRIMARY checkout with a durable launch path, 2 test gate (detect, measure a baseline in a detached tree, parallelism), 3 import (existing import-existing-project), priorities from a handoff doc, deps for phase-gate tasks, 4 workflow cutover (rulebook sections that write the imported files -> ddflow commands; config from rulebook conventions: forbidden trailers, weekly cadences, sibling repos, live vs journal changelog), 5 freeze the imported files, 6 harness (enabledMcpjsonServers, SessionStart hook, git hooks, machine-local reviewers), 7 verify end to end and commit. Later tasks turn stages into tools; this one makes the whole path exist now.
data.title: An 'onboard' workflow command (MCP prompt): the one path from 'MCP attached' to a verified cutover, asking the operator at each decision; the handshake of an unadopted or half-cut-over repo points to it
Onboarding preflight: report leftover git/harness worktrees, branches and stashes as merged (--is-ancestor) or holding unique work; remove merged ones only on apply
Onboarding test gate: detect the runner, measure a baseline in a detached clean tree, propose unit_tests (with parallelism, e.g. pytest-xdist) and a live_test smoke

Onboarding cutover: find rulebook lines (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/commands, handoff docs) that tell agents to write the imported files; propose the ddflow replacement per line; generate the freeze ratchet (a pre-commit local hook where the framework is used, else a test)

Onboarding harness: enabledMcpjsonServers for the registered servers, machine-local reviewers.toml/gates.toml copied from a sibling project and git-ignored, a 'ddflow' shell command on the harness PATH when the MCP is PYTHONPATH-pinned
Onboarding imports the agent harness's own per-project memory (Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/*.md) as ddflow memory records, deduplicated, with the operator's OK

'ddflow onboard --verify': a live MCP handshake from the REGISTERED entry, hooks armed (and a forbidden-trailer probe refused), brief/next non-empty, freeze ratchet present, frozen files unchanged since import, suite green -- one report

data.summary: init writes .ddflow/.gitignore without reviewers.toml and gates.toml, so a project adopted today commits its machine-local reviewer endpoints (LAN IPs) and machine-sized gate settings on the first 'git add .ddflow' (found by the rubber-duck of B-onboard-command; home-simulator got the lines by hand)
